subject: modeling a cyclic phase shift parameter

messages.author: 63620ab6a688da19
messages.subject: modeling a cyclic phase shift parameter
parts:
Hi there,

I have a (pretty much working) periodic time series model where I'm estimating a linear combination of a harmonic basis from some data.  Normalizing the period and phase units vs. the data, I'm using Stan to sample likelihood distributions of amplitude and phase for each harmonic; the periods are a fixed value divided by powers of 2.  At the moment I'm using prior knowledge about the phase (which ranges from 0 to 1 -- the 2pi factor is being accounted for) and using a Beta prior to keep the system about where I think it should be and push away from 0 or 1.  I'm getting a decent fit between the PPC and my data, and the chains are converging well.

Q: How do I relax this prior to be U(0,1) and tell the HMC random step to let it "wrap around" freely at the ends, or get a similar effect?

The effect of the phase is of course cyclic and the fractional part in (0,1) is all that matters, i.e. the mantissa.  I don't want to rely on useful prior knowledge about the phase, and I'd rather use a U(0,1) prior where the HMC random step is allowed to wrap around off either end, so that it can shift each harmonic in either direction from any initial guess, and explore the space without penalties near 0 or 1 because those will sometimes be the best answers.

It seems like this is something that HMC should be able to cope with trivially but I'm not sure how to express it, and I would guess someone has done this kind of a model before but didn't see such a trick in the forum or the stan reference manual.  Maybe by allowing an unconstrained phase to vary arbitrarily over the reals, give it a fairly flat N(.5, 3) prior or some such, and use only the mantissa of the result as a variable in the hierarchical model to judge convergence?  Is there any direct way to tell stan "real<lower=0,upper=1,wrap=true>"?  Maybe a different representation of the phase would be better?

Any suggestions on how to accomplish this would be appreciated.  Thanks in advance.

thanks,
Hamilton

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling a cyclic phase shift parameter
parts:
The problem is that in an amplitude/phase basis the phase is an element 
of S^{1} which cannot be mapped into the real line and hence cannot be
run immediately in Stan.  Hamiltonian Monte Carlo itself can handle these 
topologies just fine, we just don’t support them in Stan at the moment.  

Although it’s difficult to implement new topologies like spheres and
torii and such into Stan generally, they’re straightforward to add in
a bespoke fashion if you’re up for coding your own implementation of
HMC.  See http://arxiv.org/abs/1301.6064 for details.

Alternatively, just switch to a sin+cos basis which can be fit directly in Stan.

The next release (2.10) should finally fix the unit
vectors (for hyperspherical parameters). We use the Marsaglia
trick of generating K unit normals and then projecting down
to the surface of a sphere. I don't know if that's helpful.

- Bob
